title: Nail extractor
prompt: a nail extractor gripping a partly driven nail in a wood block on a table with three buttons: “Grip” seats the claw beneath the nail head; “Pull” pivots the tool against the wood and draws out the nail; “Reset” replaces the nail for another pull; see-through reveals the claw contact, fulcrum and effort and load arms
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation shows a forked nail extractor magnifying hand effort as its heel rocks against wood.

identity.note: Levers / Levers in action / First-class levers / Nail extractor, page 22. Hand effort about contact with the wood overcomes nail extraction resistance.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct from hammer. Extraction magnifies force about contact with the wood. Striking on page 23 magnifies head travel about the wrist. Keep Strike out of this brief.

prompt.note: The current Nail extractor title and extraction-only prompt are faithful. The saved 2016 page image confirms the label. Retain claw-hammer only as the legacy identifier. Reset is staged specimen replacement, not an automatic nail-insertion mechanism.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

representativeConstruction.basis: Forged carbon steel, contoured bar, polished beveled cutting edges and nail slots. Geometry is a schematic one-ended nail extractor, not a product replica.

teachingAdaptation.fixtures: Wood block, partly driven short nail and tabletop stage the source example.
teachingAdaptation.Grip: Slides the fork beneath the nail head.
teachingAdaptation.Pull: Prescribed rolling heel and claw contact raise and tilt the nail until its point clears the wood.
teachingAdaptation.Reset: Stages replacement of the specimen and returns the tool. No automatic insertion mechanism is claimed.
teachingAdaptation.overlays: Effort and nail resistance arrows, fulcrum and vertical-force moment arms are diagrams, not anatomy.
teachingAdaptation.scale: One model unit represents 3 mm. Nail lift is vertical head displacement, not extraction force.
teachingAdaptation.limits: Wood compression, bending and friction are omitted. No quantitative force prediction. No page caption.
